agency.name: Oklahoma Department of Mental Health and Substance Abuse Services (ODMHSAS)

narrNote: Confirmed on NARR's official affiliates page (narronline.org/affiliates), which states verbatim that the Oklahoma Alliance for Recovery Resources (OKARR) is the Oklahoma state affiliate of the National Alliance for Recovery Residences (NARR). OKARR was incubated with ODMHSAS support under an MOU (the current nonprofit dates to 2024, succeeding the affiliate effort launched in 2020) and certifies Oklahoma recovery residences to NARR standards; certification is voluntary, but OKARR certification is required for ODMHSAS Recovery Housing Scholarship funds, and OKARR maintains the statewide certified-housing locator referenced by ODMHSAS. Caution: some third-party sources expand OKARR as 'Recovery Residences' - NARR's and OKARR's own wording is 'Resources', which is used here.
notes: ODMHSAS is Oklahoma's SAMHSA-designated Single State Agency; its oklahoma.gov hub (fetched and content-verified in this run) states the department oversees all prevention, treatment and education for mental health and substance abuse in the state. The agency phone is the ODMHSAS headquarters number published in the department's official FFY24-25 block grant application hosted on oklahoma.gov. Medicaid: SoonerCare, Oklahoma's Medicaid program run by the Oklahoma Health Care Authority (OHCA), lists substance abuse detoxification and substance abuse treatments among covered benefits on its official consumer FAQs page (fetched and verified in this run; SoonerCare helpline 800-987-7767). County-level lookup: ODMHSAS designates the Network of Care services directory (oklahoma.networkofcare.org) as its official directory searchable by county and ZIP in the department's own Network of Care instructions, but that site returned HTTP 403 to this run's verification fetch and its content could not be verified, so countyDirectory is null rather than asserted unverified. 211 Oklahoma covers all 77 counties and is operated by HeartLine, Inc. for the western half of the state and Tulsa Area United Way for the eastern half (per its site, verified live). Peer organizations: OCARTA is Oklahoma's peer-run recovery community organization (founded 2002, funded in part by ODMHSAS, verified live), and Mental Health Association Oklahoma operates peer-to-peer recovery services and the state's two peer-run drop-in centers (verified live). All URLs in this file were fetched in-run on 2026-10-22 and returned HTTP 200 with matching content, except the countyDirectory item documented above.
